intro: White Plains is the county seat and commercial hub of Westchester County, with a high-rise downtown of offices, retail, and apartments.
localFacts: ["County seat of Westchester County and home to its government center and courts", "A major stop on Metro-North's Harlem Line, roughly 35 minutes from Grand Central", "Downtown functions as Westchester's principal office and shopping district"]

name: Ramapo
intro: The Town of Ramapo is Rockland County's most populous town, in the county's southwest along the New Jersey border, including Suffern, Monsey, and Spring Valley.
localFacts: ["The most populous town in Rockland County", "Includes the villages of Suffern, Spring Valley (in part), Airmont, and New Square", "The Ramapo Mountains and Harriman State Park lands rise along the town's edge"]

name: Clarkstown
intro: The Town of Clarkstown occupies central Rockland County and includes New City, the county seat, along with Nanuet and Congers.
localFacts: ["New City, the Rockland County seat, is within the town", "The Palisades Center in West Nyack is one of the largest shopping malls in the country", "Rockland Lake State Park sits along the town's Hudson River side"]

name: Orangetown
intro: The Town of Orangetown covers Rockland County's southeastern corner along the Hudson River and New Jersey border, including Nyack, Pearl River, and Orangeburg.
localFacts: ["The village of Nyack is a well-known Hudson riverfront downtown near the Mario M. Cuomo Bridge", "Borders New Jersey, with Pearl River on the Pascack Valley commuter rail line", "Hook Mountain and Nyack Beach state parks line the Hudson shore"]

name: Haverstraw
intro: The Town of Haverstraw sits on the Hudson River in northern Rockland County, including the villages of Haverstraw and West Haverstraw.
localFacts: ["The Hudson River reaches its widest point, Haverstraw Bay, along the town's shore", "The riverfront village of Haverstraw was historically a major brickmaking center", "High Tor and part of Harriman State Park rise behind the riverfront"]

name: Stony Point
intro: The Town of Stony Point is Rockland County's northernmost town, a largely residential community on the west bank of the Hudson River.
localFacts: ["Stony Point Battlefield, site of a 1779 Revolutionary War battle, is a state historic site on the Hudson", "Bear Mountain and Harriman state park lands cover much of the town's western area", "The northernmost and least populous of Rockland's five towns"]
